title: Needle in the Log Stack
summary: Someone is trying to break into DotTech's server. The answer is hidden in a log file with 1,500 lines.
briefing:
Alarm bells at DotTech! Someone has been trying to log in to the main server, dottech-srv, all night long.

Every login attempt is written to the server's log file, `/var/log/auth.log`. The problem: it has 1,500 lines. Reading it line by line would take forever.

IT believes the attacker slipped up and left a clue in the log. Your job is to find that one line – without reading them all.
objective: Search /var/log/auth.log and find the line that contains the flag.
debrief:
Excellent detective work! `grep` searches inside files and only shows the lines that match – it found one line among 1,500 in an instant.

Security analysts use `grep` every day to dig through logs. Try `grep -i` to ignore case, `grep -n` to see line numbers, or a pipe: `cat /var/log/auth.log | grep Failed`.

The lesson for DotTech: logs are gold. Keep them, and learn how to search them.
hints: A log file records events, one per line. This one is far too long to read by hand – you need a tool that searches inside files.
Use `grep <text> <file>` to show only the lines that contain some text. Think about it: what does every flag start with?

mails.subject: URGENT: someone is knocking
mails.body:
Hi! Jonas from IT here. Someone has been trying to log in to dottech-srv ALL NIGHT. Every attempt is in `/var/log/auth.log`, but it's 1,500 lines and I have three other fires to put out.

I think the attacker slipped up and left something in the log. Can you find it? Mission: **Needle in the Log Stack**.

Jonas

mails.subject: Re: URGENT: someone is knocking
mails.body:
One `grep` and you found it?! I was going to scroll through it line by line tonight.

I owe you a coffee. Possibly several.

Jonas

lines: Thousands of failed logins on dottech-srv since midnight.
Please investigate. Tip from IT: don't read the whole file – search it!
